Subject: Quick Q: where our inference requests are processed and how deletion works

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. Before we kick off a short pilot we need a concise explanation for our security and procurement teams about exactly where MedSol traffic will be executed and how you handle deletion/retention. They asked for:  

- A high-level execution topology (regions, fallback regions, and any transient hops).
- List of subprocessors that may touch inference payloads (and what they do).
- Data retention windows for request/response logs, KV caches, and any telemetry.
- The deletion playbook: what happens when we ask for erasure (timelines, who confirms, proof).

Can you send a short Q&A we can attach to our purchase request? If there’s a diagram, that would help.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Reed
Director, Cloud Architecture — MedSol Health

Hi Sam — great to hear. I put together a concise playbook below; Jordan and Karthik are copied for technical and subprocessor details. I’ll attach a simplified diagram and a processing matrix after this message.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Execution: Primary execution in customer-selected region (us-east-1 or europe-west-1) when available; automatic routing to a regional fallback (same continent) if capacity constrained. Transient hops occur to our CDN and control-plane for routing only; payload processing happens on GPUs in the serving region.
- Subprocessors: Storage for logs (S3/GCS equivalents), monitoring (metrics/alerts), and a managed orchestration provider may touch metadata. We do not persist customer request payloads outside the selected region except for short-lived telemetry needed to route and batch (see retention below).
- Retention: Request/response logs: 30 days by default (configurable down to 0), KV cache TTL is workload-configurable (default 24 hours), telemetry and traces: 90 days for platform analytics.
- Deletion: Customer/CS/Legal triggers an erasure request -> automated purge runs across primary storage and caches within 72 hours -> confirmation package generated (hashes/manifest) within 7 business days.

I’ll follow up with the diagram and a CSV mapping of subprocessors and their processing role. Let me know if MedSol needs a stricter retention SLAs or on-prem/private deployment options.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sam — adding technical detail to Vanessa’s summary. I’ll keep it succinct.

1) Execution topology specifics
- Inbound: Customer client -> public API endpoint in requested region (TLS 1.3).
- Control-plane: Small control-plane API may be routed via our control region for authentication and routing decisions; no inference tokens are executed there.
- Serving plane: Actual model inference (KV cache, attention compute) occurs on GPUs provisioned in the serving region you select (us-east-1 by default).
- Fallbacks: If the requested region is saturated, policy routes to the nearest compatible region (e.g., us-west-2) according to routing rules you can set (latency-first / cost-first / pinned). These fallbacks are within the same legal jurisdiction unless you opt into cross-jurisdiction failover.

2) Subprocessors and what they touch
- Object storage provider (regional buckets) — stores transient logs and batching artifacts; data-at-rest encrypted with customer-managed keys when requested.
- Metrics pipeline (aggregated telemetry) — only ingest metrics and anonymized traces; request payloads are trimmed before forwarding.
- Orchestration partner — runs the scheduling layer; has metadata about job ids and region but not full request payloads.
- SSO/KMS providers (for customers who integrate) — may see metadata for key usage but not plaintext payloads.

We maintain an up-to-date CSV (attached) listing vendor names, regions they operate in, and the minimum set of data they may process. If MedSol requires any subprocessor exclusions, we can discuss a custom contract or Dedicated/Private deployment.

3) Deletion playbook (steps and evidence)
- Step 0 (Request): CS or customer submits erasure ticket in our portal + signed request for legal retention exceptions if any.
- Step 1 (Identification): We run account-scoped queries to locate primary artifacts: region buckets, cache keys, trace indices.
- Step 2 (Purge): Automated purge pipeline clears buckets, invalidates KV keys, and rotates any ephemeral caches. Default SLA: purge actions complete within 72 hours.
- Step 3 (Verification & Audit): For full-proof, we generate a deletion manifest (object IDs, timestamps, cryptographic hashes) and return a signed confirmation within 7 business days. For enterprise customers we can run a co-signed verification with your audit team.

4) Edge cases
- Backups: Nightly backups are disabled for hosted tokens by default; if you enable backups we will include them in the purge flow.
- Logs forwarded to third-party SIEMs: if configured, you must request deletion from that SIEM and provide proof; we will assist with a transfer manifest.

Happy to run through this on a quick call if you want a diagram walkthrough.

—Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa/Jordan — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and security:  

1) When routing to a fallback region, do you ever route across legal jurisdictions without explicit customer consent? MedSol cannot permit cross-jurisdiction processing for PHI.
2) For the deletion manifest, will the hashes prove that the exact objects were removed (we need cryptographic evidence for our auditors)?

If those two are yes/clear we can move to a pilot contract.

Sam

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where our inference requests are processed and how deletion works

Sam — short answers and next steps.

1) Cross-jurisdiction routing: No, we will not route across legal jurisdictions for accounts that opt-out. By default the fallback is intra-jurisdiction (same country/EEA/US region). For PHI workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment; we’ll add a binding routing policy to the pilot to ensure strict locality.

2) Deletion manifest and cryptographic evidence: Yes — our manifest includes object IDs, deletion timestamps, and SHA-256 hashes computed before deletion. The manifest is signed by our key and can be co-signed or cross-checked by a mutually-trusted auditor.

Next steps: I’ve attached the short playbook diagram and the processing matrix CSV. If MedSol is comfortable I’ll open a pilot SOW (30 days, limited ops data retention) and include the routing policy in Appendix A.

I’ll also create a one-page note for procurement that summarizes the two commitments above. Do you want that in a separate PDF?

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
